shared.how_captured: `pnpm capture` (scripts/capture.ts), in a copy of the checkout with a throwaway Postgres and a local site of its own (`pnpm dev:local`, every setting pretend), seeded with each state's `seed` and signed in as its `as` with `pnpm seed:cookies`. Google Chrome through Playwright, light colour scheme, Europe/Vilnius time zone, en-GB. Phone: 390 x 844, device scale factor 3, mobile and touch, as an iPhone of that width renders a page (PNG 1170 px wide). Desktop: 1280 x 800, scale 1. Full-page screenshots taken after every streamed part had arrived, fonts had loaded and animations had finished. Next.js's development badge is hidden; nothing else is changed. Requests to anywhere but the local site are answered with a blank stand-in page, so an opened Award board shows an empty frame. A path's {sunday} is the latest Sunday whose Matchday has started, and {sunday-N} the Sunday N weeks before it, as the seed dates every scenario from the day it runs. A state with `databaseStopped` is taken with the local database stopped; one with `minutesIntoLatestMatchday` with the local site's clock moved to that many minutes after the latest Matchday's start, as a Matchday starts only on Sunday at 20:00 and no seed can put one under way at another time. The notes and the descriptions were written from the screenshots of 25 November 2026, and their dates are that day's. Settings that are set locally but may not be on the live site change some pages: the Telegram invite link (home page, /welcome/profile), the Organiser's contact address (footer, /privacy) and the scheduled jobs (/organiser).
shared.page_frame: Every page is one column inside a frame: header, the page's <main>, footer. The paper background (#f4f1ea), ink text (#111), one marigold accent (#e4a23a) used only for the small rotated square that marks 'what is happening now', Newsreader (serif) for headings and the system sans-serif for text, body text 17 px. The content is at most 1088 px wide (68rem) with a side gutter of 21 px on a 390 px phone and 96 px each side at 1280. Most pages keep their text in a narrower column on the left at desktop width (608 px); the home page uses the full width. A dark colour scheme exists (prefers-color-scheme: dark) and was not captured.

pages.name: Home
pages.who: Anyone. A visitor gets the pitch, the next Matchday (or the Season 1 countdown) and 'Sign in with LinkedIn'. Someone part-way through signing up gets 'Signed in as' and 'Finish signing up'. A Member gets 'Your Profile', 'Edit your Profile', the Telegram group's invite link and, once the tournament exists on Lichess, the link to the Matchday. The Organiser gets exactly what a Member gets.
pages.purpose: For a visitor: read in a few sentences what Offboard is, see when the next Matchday is (or how many more sign-ups Season 1 is waiting for) and decide whether to join. For a Member: the way to this Sunday's Matchday on Lichess, to their own Profile and to the Telegram group.
pages.should_be_able_to: A visitor: decide it is for them and press 'Sign in with LinkedIn'. A Member: open this Sunday's Matchday on Lichess.
on_it_now: Eyebrow 'Free chess Club · Vilnius', heading 'Sunday chess for people in tech', a four-sentence lede (working in tech is busy and lonely; every Sunday evening we play chess online; with luck some of us become friends).

Status card (to the right of the heading at desktop width, under the lede on a phone), one of: 'Season 1 · N more Members to go' and how Season 1 starts; 'Next Matchday · Sunday 29 November at 20:00'; for a Member, 'Matchday under way' with 'Lichess lets you join until round 3 starts.' until 90 minutes after 20:00. A Member also gets 'Join this Matchday on Lichess' once the tournament exists.

Under the card, for a visitor: the 'Sign in with LinkedIn' button and a note that signing in lets Offboard store the LinkedIn name, photo and email, with a 'Privacy and terms' link. For anyone signed in: photo or initials, 'Signed in as <name>', 'Sign out'; then 'Finish signing up' (part-way) or 'Your Profile' (filled button), 'Edit your Profile' (outlined) and 'Telegram group' (Member).
'The chess': one paragraph (20:00 Vilnius time on Lichess, 5 minutes a side plus 3 seconds a move, any level, best four of six Matchdays).

'Meeting people': one paragraph: what a Profile can say, the Telegram group ('A Telegram group to talk in is still to come.' when no invite link is set), and no selling or recruiting unless a Profile invites it.

'Leaderboards and Recaps': 'Both are public and show your name.'; from a Season's sixth Matchday until the next Season's first, a marked line '<name> is the Season N champion.' (or '<names> share the Season N title.'); links 'This Season's Leaderboard', 'All-time Leaderboard' and 'Recaps'.
At desktop width each section after the first is a row: heading on the left third, text on the right.
leads_from: The 'Offboard' logo link in the header of every page, and 'Home' in the back links of most pages.
LinkedIn sign-in, for a returning person (a new person goes to /welcome).
'Sign out'; 'Save and continue' and 'Skip for now' on /welcome/profile; 'Home' on /left.

Redirects: a visitor opening any signed-in page (/profiles/<id>, /profile, /profile/leave, /welcome...) is sent here after a 1-second refresh; a Member opening /welcome or /welcome/lichess, and someone who has agreed but not connected Lichess opening /welcome, are sent here.
leads_to: 'Join this Matchday on Lichess' → the tournament on lichess.org (new tab), Members only.
'Finish signing up' → /welcome or /welcome/lichess, whichever step is next.
'Your Profile' → /profiles/<own id>; 'Edit your Profile' → /profile; 'Telegram group' → t.me invite (new tab).
Champion line 'Season N' → /seasons/N; 'This Season's Leaderboard' → /seasons; 'All-time Leaderboard' → /all-time; 'Recaps' → /recaps.

pages.name: Edit your Profile
pages.who: Members only. A visitor is sent home (a 200 with the heading 'Edit your Profile' showing until a 1-second refresh); part-way people go to their next step.
pages.purpose: Where a Member changes or clears the optional parts of their Profile, switches to another Lichess account, or starts leaving the Club.
pages.should_be_able_to: Change their Company, position, LinkedIn link or open-to line and save.
on_it_now: Heading 'Edit your Profile', lede (Members see the name and photo from LinkedIn and anything added here).

A panel with four fields, each with a label and all but LinkedIn profile link with a hint: Company website, Position (up to 80 characters), LinkedIn profile link, Open to (up to 140 characters); 'Save changes'. A refused entry shows a red message above its field and keeps what was typed.
'Your Lichess account': 'You play as <username> on Lichess.', how switching works, a problem message after a failed switch, 'Switch Lichess account' button.
'Leave the Club': 'Delete your account' button.
Back links: 'See your Profile as Members see it', Home.
leads_from: A failed Lichess switch returns here with ?lichess=<problem>.
leads_to: 'Switch Lichess account' → lichess.org → own Profile, or back here with a problem.
phone_facts: No sideways scroll.
Text fields are 285 px wide with 261 px for text: the saved LinkedIn link needs 525 px and the saved open-to line 406 px, so both are cut off at the field's edge.
'Pretend--Ana' (the Lichess username) is a link 118.8 x 20 px in running text; 'Home' 40.7 x 44.
Every button and field is at least 44 px tall.
No text under 14 px outside the footer.
differs_from_spec: Spec: a Member edits Company, position, LinkedIn link and open-to line; built as one form here plus the Lichess switch and the way out of the Club on the same page.
After 'Save changes' the Member is taken to their Profile rather than kept on the form; there is no 'saved' message.

'Agree and continue' button.
'Rather not join? Delete your account.'

pages.name: Organiser
pages.who: The Organiser only. A visitor with no session gets a real 404 and the not-found page; anyone else signed in (a Member or someone part-way) gets the not-found page under a 200, with the tab titled 'Page not found'.
pages.purpose: The Organiser's one place to see whether the site is creating Matchdays, collecting results and posting to Telegram, and to act: skip a Sunday, set a Season's start, remove a Member, renew the Lichess permission, and clear up what the site could not do on Lichess.
pages.should_be_able_to: See at a glance whether anything needs them, and act on it.
on_it_now: Eyebrow 'Only you can see this page', heading 'Organiser'.
A notice after removing a Member ('Member removed.') or a refusal.
'Next Matchday' card: the date, and whether it is on Lichess ('Open it on Lichess'), when it will be created, or a red alert saying what stops it.
'Lichess permission': account, connected and expiry dates, an alert when expired or unreadable, how to connect, 'Connect Lichess' / 'Connect Lichess again'.
'Cancel on Lichess' (only when there are some): Sundays no longer Matchdays whose tournaments the site could not cancel, each with why, 'Cancel it on Lichess' and 'Done'.
'Remove from the Lichess team' (only when there are some): accounts the site could not remove, each with why and 'Done', and 'Remove members on Lichess'.
'Schedule': 'Upcoming Sundays', the next eight with their Season and Matchday and a 'Skip' or 'Undo' button; 'Season start' with a Season select, a 'First Matchday' date field and 'Set start'.
'Remove a Member': a select 'Choose a Member' (name and Lichess username) and 'Continue'.
'Telegram': what the bot does or a red alert about its settings; 'Send a test message to me', 'Send a test message to the group'.

'Scheduled jobs': Creating Matchdays, Collecting results, Posting to Telegram, Backing up, Alerting you, each with outcome and last run or a red 'Not run yet' alert; 'Results not in' when a Matchday's results are missing; 'Last failure' (job, began, since, detail) or 'No job has failed.'
Back link: Home. Every panel is a bordered box.
leads_from: Nothing on the site links here: the Organiser types the address.
/organiser/remove: 'Keep them', 'Back to the Organiser page', and after a removal.
Connecting the Organiser's Lichess account returns here.
leads_to: 'Open it on Lichess', 'Cancel it on Lichess', 'Remove members on Lichess', the account link (new tabs).
Skip, Undo, Set start, Done and the test messages stay on this page.
phone_facts: No sideways scroll.

The Season select's chosen option ('Season 4, now from Sunday 27 December') needs 319 px and the select has 265 px, so it is cut off; in season-over 'Season 3, now from Sunday 17 January' needs 298 px.

Links under 44 px: the Lichess account 114.5 x 20, 'Cancel it on Lichess' 166.3 x 20, 'Remove members on Lichess' 237.1 x 20, 'Home' 40.7 x 44. All buttons, selects and fields are at least 44 px tall.
3,407 px tall before Season 1, 5,078 px in club, 6,135 px with failures (4 to 7 screens).
13 px text: the eyebrow, the 'Next Matchday' label and the footer.
differs_from_spec: Spec and ticket #16: one page with three actions (remove a Member, skip a Matchday, set a Season's start) that shows the permission's expiry and the last failure. As built it also has: the next Matchday's status, undoing a skip, Telegram test messages, the state of five scheduled jobs, results not in, and two lists of things to do by hand on Lichess (from tickets #13, #15, #17, #44).
Removing a Member is confirmed on a page of its own (/organiser/remove).
Nothing links to the page; the spec does not say whether anything should.
